# Lazy loading and content behind interactions

Day 2 confirms Day 1's point that Google's crawlers do not click and adds that they do not scroll either: content that loads only after a click or a scroll is not in the DOM when Google renders the page, so it cannot be indexed. What counts is presence in the DOM, not visibility: tab or accordion content hidden with CSS or the hidden attribute can be indexed, while tab content fetched from an API on click does not exist for Google. Instead of scrolling, Google renders in a tall viewport, about 10,000 pixels according to Google's speaker (a figure not in the documentation, which calls it viewport expansion and warns it can miss infinite content), so content loaded when an element enters the viewport, for example with an Intersection Observer, loads while scroll-event listeners never run. For infinite scroll, Google's lazy-loading guide asks for paginated loading, with a persistent URL for each chunk, sequential links between them and the History API updating the displayed URL, a concrete pattern to go with Day 1's caution that 'load more' pagination is risky.

Based on: `D1-C115`, `D2-C195`, `D2-C268`, `D2-C271`, `D2-C197`, `D2-C196`, `D2-C202`, `D2-C201`, `D2-C272`, `D2-C273`, `D2-C200`, `D2-C199`, `D2-C274`, `D2-C198`, `D2-C276`, `D1-C114`.

## What to do

- Put tab and accordion content in the initial DOM and hide it with CSS instead of fetching it on click.
- Trigger lazy loading with an Intersection Observer or native lazy loading, never with a scroll event listener.
- Give infinite-scroll and 'load more' lists paginated URLs linked with `<a href>`.
- Treat the 10,000-pixel viewport as a safety margin, not a target.

## What Google's documentation says

- **[Docs]** In Google's March 2023 SEO office hours, John Mueller said Google handles infinite scroll with viewport expansion, rendering a page like a very long phone, which is not very efficient and can miss content, so pagination links are strongly recommended.
  > "this is done through a technique called "viewport expansion", where we render a page like a very long phone."
  <br><sub>`D2-C200` · Google Search Central (SEO office hours transcript, March 2023) · annotates Day 2, Lightning session D: Rendering and JavaScript · is the documentation · [March 2023 Google SEO office hours](https://developers.google.com/search/help/office-hours/2023/march)</sub>

- **[Docs]** Google's March 2023 SEO office hours say Google sees infinite-scroll content through viewport expansion, rendering a page like a very long phone, which is not particularly efficient and can miss infinite content.
  > "a technique called "viewport expansion", where we render a page like a very long phone"
  <br><sub>`D2-C273` · Google Search Central (SEO office hours transcript, March 2023) · annotates Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript · is the documentation · [March 2023 Google SEO office hours](https://developers.google.com/search/help/office-hours/2023/march) · Used by `DEV-URL-07`, the glossary term *Viewport expansion*</sub>

- **[Docs]** To make infinite scroll indexable, Google's lazy-loading guide says to support paginated loading: give each chunk its own persistent, unique URL, link sequentially to those URLs, and update the displayed URL with the History API when a new chunk becomes the main visible element.
  <br><sub>`D2-C276` · Google Search Central · annotates Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript · is the documentation · [Fix lazy-loaded content](https://developers.google.com/search/docs/crawling-indexing/javascript/lazy-loading) · Extends [D1-C115](../../40-sessions/day1/D1-S00-day-1-session-not-recorded.md) · Used by `DEV-URL-07`</sub>

## Analysis

- **[Analysis]** Audit tabs, accordions and 'load more' lists for content fetched on click or scroll: put tab content in the initial DOM and hide it with CSS, trigger lazy loading with an Intersection Observer, and give long lists paginated URLs linked with `<a href>`.
  <br><sub>`D2-C203` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, Lightning session D: Rendering and JavaScript</sub>

- **[Analysis]** Treat the 10,000-pixel viewport as a safety margin, not a target: load lazy content when it enters the viewport (Intersection Observer or native lazy loading, never scroll listeners), and give infinite-scroll content paginated URLs linked with `<a href>` so anything below the first rendered screen stays reachable.
  <br><sub>`D2-C275` · Ibrahim Anjro (author) · annotates Day 2, What is Google friendly JavaScript</sub>

## Built on these claims

The items of the developer and content kits that rest on this topic's claims.

- Requirement `DEV-REN-02`: Have all indexable content in the DOM after load, without clicks, typing or scrolling
- Requirement `DEV-REN-03`: Lazy-load with native lazy loading or an IntersectionObserver, never with scroll events
- Requirement `DEV-URL-07`: Back infinite scroll and load-more buttons with paginated URLs
- Glossary term *Lazy loading*
- Glossary term *Viewport expansion*
